value.body: Explains insurance policies — life, health, motor and other general cover — to customers, helps them choose a plan, completes the paperwork and supports them at renewal and claim time. Advisors work as licensed agents of an insurer, as employees of insurers or brokers, or through banks that sell insurance (bancassurance). Much of the day is meeting or calling customers and following up on leads.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: Class 12 minimum for agents; graduates for most salaried roles

items.label: Licence
items.value: Registration as an insurance agent under IRDAI rules
items.note: Requires prescribed training and passing the IC-38 exam

items.label: Pay structure
items.value: Commission for agents; salary plus incentives for employees

items.label: Individual insurance agents
items.note: As on 31 March 2025; up about 8% in a year

items.label: Agents' share of life individual new-business premium

value.title: How you get in
value.body: The most direct route is to be sponsored by an insurer as an agent, complete the prescribed training and pass the IC-38 exam. Graduates also join insurance companies, brokers or banks as sales officers or relationship executives, often through walk-in or campus hiring. Salaried freshers usually work against monthly sales targets.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Explaining policy terms in plain language

value.title: At a glance
items: Agent income is largely commission-based and can vary month to month.
Mis-selling is regulated; advice is expected to match the customer's needs.
Growth path: advisor → team leader or sales manager, or a move into underwriting, claims or broking; Insurance Institute of India qualifications support technical moves.
